questions.question: Which statement best captures the primary aim of development testing as described in the text?

options.A: To verify that the software meets all performance requirements.
options.B: To discover bugs in the software.
options.C: To document the software architecture for future maintenance.
options.D: To ensure the user interface complies with design standards.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] Development testing is primarily a defect testing process whose aim is to discover bugs in the software. [Page 41]

---

questions.question: How does the text describe the relationship between development testing and debugging?

options.A: Testing is performed after all debugging activities are completed.
options.B: Testing replaces the need for debugging.
options.C: Testing is usually interleaved with debugging.
options.D: Debugging is only required when testing fails to find any defects.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] The text states that development testing is usually interleaved with debugging—the process of locating problems and fixing them. [Page 41]

---

questions.question: According to the passage, which of the following is a limitation of software testing?

options.A: Testing can guarantee that no defects remain in the software.
options.B: Testing can demonstrate that the software will behave correctly in every possible circumstance.
options.C: Testing may miss some inputs or scenarios that could reveal additional problems.
options.D: Testing eliminates the need for future maintenance.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] The text explains that testing cannot demonstrate that software is defect‑free or will behave as specified in every circumstance, and overlooked tests may discover further problems. [Page 36]

---

questions.question: The text lists several types of undesirable system behavior that testing seeks to root out. Which of the following is **not** mentioned as one of those behaviors?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] Undesirable behaviors cited include system crashes, unwanted interactions, incorrect computations, and data corruption; poor scalability is not listed. [Page 36]

---

questions.question: When a tester finds an input sequence that causes the software to behave incorrectly, what is the underlying cause as defined in the text?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] The passage states that incorrect or undesirable behavior caused by inputs is due to defects (bugs) in the software. [Page 36]

---

questions.question: Which of the following best reflects Dijkstra’s view on the purpose of testing, as quoted in the material?

options.A: Testing is primarily a means to validate user satisfaction.
options.B: Testing is a way to confirm that the software meets all performance metrics.
options.C: Testing aims to root out undesirable system behavior such as crashes and data corruption.
options.D: Testing guarantees that the software will never fail after release.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Dijkstra’s quote emphasizes that testing seeks to root out undesirable behavior like crashes, unwanted interactions, incorrect computations, and data corruption. [Page 36]

---

questions.question: In the context of unit testing (8.1.1), which of the following activities aligns most closely with its objective?

options.A: Evaluating the entire system’s response to real‑world traffic.
options.B: Verifying that individual code modules behave as specified.
options.C: Conducting usability surveys with end users.
options.D: Performing load testing on the database server.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] Unit testing focuses on testing individual units (code modules) to ensure they work as intended, consistent with the definition in section 8.1.1. [Page 36]

---

questions.question: According to the passage, why is it impossible for testing to prove that software is completely defect‑free?

options.A: Because defects can only be identified during production use.
options.B: Because testing can only cover a finite set of inputs and scenarios.
options.C: Because developers intentionally leave hidden bugs.
options.D: Because testing tools are inherently inaccurate.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] The text notes that testing cannot demonstrate defect‑free software because it is always possible that an overlooked test could reveal further problems, implying limited coverage of inputs/scenarios. [Page 36]

---

questions.question: Which of the following best illustrates the concept of “interleaved” testing and debugging described in the material?

options.A: Completing all test cases first, then fixing all discovered bugs in a separate phase.
options.B: Writing code, immediately testing it, fixing any defects found, and then repeating the cycle.
options.C: Skipping testing until the final system integration stage.
options.D: Delegating debugging to a separate team that works after testing is finished.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] “Interleaved” means testing and debugging occur together in an iterative cycle—test, locate problems, fix, and repeat. [Page 41]

---

questions.question: The passage mentions that testing seeks to find inputs where the software’s behavior is “incorrect, undesirable, or does not conform to its specification.” Which of the following scenarios would **most directly** satisfy this description?

options.A: The software’s UI theme colors do not match the brand guide.
options.B: The application crashes when a user uploads a file larger than 10 MB.
options.C: The development team uses a programming language they are unfamiliar with.
options.D: The project deadline is extended due to resource constraints.

questions.explanation: [Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] A crash caused by a specific input (large file) is an example of incorrect or undesirable behavior that does not conform to specification. [Page 36]
